source_text: Sed agnoscimus adimpleri propheticam vocem Simeonis super adhuc recentem infantem dominum pronuntiatam: Ecce hic positus est in ruinam et suscitationem multorum in IsraÃ«l, et in signum, quod contradicetur. Signum enim nativitatis Christi secundum Esaiam: Propterea dabit vobis dominus ipse signum: Ecce virgo concipiet in utero, et pariet filium. Agnoscimus ergo signum contradicibile, conceptum et partum virginis Mariae, de quo Academici isti: Peperit et non peperit, virgo et non virgo; quasi non, etsi ita dicendum esset, a nobis magis dici conveniret. Peperit enim, quae ex sua carne, et non peperit, quae non ex viri semine, et virgo, quantum a viro, non virgo, quantum a partu: non tamen ut ideo non peperit, et ideo virgo quae non virgo, quia non de visceribus suis mater. Sed apud nos nihil dubium, nec retortum in ancipitem defensionem. Lux lux, et Tenebrae tenehrae, et Est est, et Non non; quod amplius, hoc a malo est. Peperit quae peperit; et si virgo concepit, in partu suo nupsit. Nam nupsit ipsa patefacti corporis lege, in quo nihil interfuit de vi masculi admissi, an emissi; idem illud sexus resignavit. Haec denique vulva est propter quam et de aliis scriptum est: Omne masculinum adaperiens vulvam sanctum vocabitur domino. Quis vere sanctus quam dei filius? Quis proprie vulvam adaperuit quam qui clausam patefecit? Ceterum omnibus nuptiae patefaciunt. Itaque magis patefacta est, quia magis erat clausa. Utique magis non virgo dicenda est quam virgo, saltu quodam mater ante quam nupta. Et quid ultra de hoc retractandum est? Cum hac ratione apostolus non ex virgine, sed ex muliere editum filium dei pronuntiavit, agnovit adapertae vulvae nuptialem passionem. Legimus quidem apud Ezechielem de vacca illa quae peperit et non peperit. Sed videte ne vos iam nunc providens spiritus sanctus notarit hac voce, disceptatures super uterum Mariae. Ceterum non contra illam suam simplicitatem pronuntiasset dubitative, Esaia dicente, Concipiet et pariet.
thought_title: The Sign of the Virgin Birth
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that Christ's flesh was truly born of Mary, and here he interprets Simeon's prophecy and Isaiah's sign to show that the virgin conception and birth are the very sign that will be contradicted.
pass_a_gloss: But we recognize [that] the prophetic voice of Simeon [is] fulfilled, pronounced over the still recent infant Lord: Behold this one is set for the ruin and raising of many in Israel, and for a sign that will be contradicted. For [it is] the sign of the birth of Christ according to Isaiah: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: Behold a virgin will conceive in the womb, and will bear a son. We recognize therefore the contradictable sign, the conception and birth of the virgin Mary, about which those Academics [say]: She bore and did not bear, virgin and not virgin; as if not, even if it had to be said thus, [it would] be more fitting [for it] to be said by us. For she bore, [she] who [bore] from her own flesh, and she did not bear, [she] who [did] not [bear] from the seed of a man, and [she is] virgin, as far as [she is] from a man, [and] not virgin, as far as [she is] from the birth: not however so that therefore she did not bear, and therefore [she is] virgin who [is] not virgin, because [she is] not mother from her own inward parts. But among us nothing [is] doubtful, nor twisted into a two-edged defense. Light [is] light, and Darkness [is] darkness, and Yes [is] yes, and No [is] no; what [is] more, this is from evil. She bore [who] bore; and if a virgin conceived, in her birth she married. For she married by the very law of the opened body, in which it made no difference whether [it was] of the force of a male admitted or emitted; that same thing unsealed the sex. This finally is the womb on account of which also about others it is written: Every male opening the womb will be called holy to the Lord. Who [is] truly holy than the Son of God? Who properly opened the womb than [he] who opened [it] closed? For the rest, marriages open [it] for all. And so it was more opened, because it was more closed. Certainly she is more to be called not virgin than virgin, by a certain leap a mother before [she was] married. And what further about this is to be handled again? Since with this reasoning the apostle proclaimed the Son of God brought forth not from a virgin, but from a woman, he recognized the nuptial passion of the opened womb. We read indeed in Ezekiel about that cow which bore and did not bear. But see [that] the Holy Spirit, already now foreseeing you, has not marked you with this voice, [as those] about to dispute over the womb of Mary. For the rest [he] would not have pronounced doubtfully against that simplicity of his, when Isaiah says, She will conceive and bear.

choices.why: Keeps the literal force of the adjective formed from contradico, matching the sign that will be contradicted in Simeon's prophecy.
Preserves Tertullian's sarcastic label for the heretics as skeptical Academics, not a neutral 'these people'.
Renders the verb literally to preserve Tertullian's provocative claim that Mary 'married' in giving birth by the law of the opened body.

choices.english: the nuptial passion of the opened womb
choices.why: Keeps 'passion' for passio to preserve the physical, bodily sense Tertullian intends, and 'nuptial' for the marriage metaphor.
rejected: the nuptial suffering of the opened womb
the wedding passion of the opened womb
the marital passion of the opened womb

choices.why: Anceps means two-edged or ambiguous; 'two-edged defense' preserves the image of a defense that cuts both ways, unlike a vague 'ambiguous defense'.
Keeps the abrupt, paradoxical force of saltus, the leap from virgin to mother before marriage.

pass_b_english: But we recognize that the prophetic voice of Simeon, pronounced over the Lord while he was still a newborn infant, is being fulfilled: "Behold, this child is set for the fall and rising of many in Israel, and for a sign that will be contradicted" (Luke 2:34). For the sign of Christ's birth, according to Isaiah, is this: "Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: Behold, a virgin will conceive in the womb and bear a son" (Isaiah 7:14). So we recognize the contradictable sign: the conception and childbearing of the virgin Mary. About this sign those Academics say, "She bore and did not bear, virgin and not virgin." As if, even if it had to be said that way, it would not be more fitting for us to say it. For she bore, because it was from her own flesh, and she did not bear, because it was not from a man's seed. And she was a virgin, as far as a man is concerned, and not a virgin, as far as giving birth is concerned. Not, however, in the sense that she therefore did not bear, and was therefore a virgin who was not a virgin, on the ground that she was not a mother from her own inward parts.

But among us nothing is doubtful, nor twisted into a two-edged defense. Light is light, and darkness is darkness, and yes is yes, and no is no; anything more than this is from evil (Matthew 5:37). She bore who bore; and if a virgin conceived, in her giving birth she married. For she married by the very law of the opened body, in which it made no difference whether the force of a male was admitted or emitted; that same sex unsealed it. This, in fact, is the womb on account of which it was also written of others: "Every male opening the womb will be called holy to the Lord" (Luke 2:23). Who is truly holy but the Son of God? Who properly opened the womb but he who opened it when it was closed? For in all other cases marriages open it. And so it was more opened, because it was more closed. Certainly she must be called not a virgin rather than a virgin, since by a kind of leap she became a mother before she was married.

And why should we argue further about this? It was with this reasoning that the apostle declared the Son of God was brought forth not from a virgin but from a woman, recognizing the marital event of the opened womb (Galatians 4:4). We do read in Ezekiel about that cow which bore and did not bear. But see whether the Holy Spirit, already foreseeing you, has not marked you with this saying, as people who would dispute about the womb of Mary. Otherwise he would not have spoken doubtfully against his own simplicity, when Isaiah says, "She will conceive and bear."

problems.why: Latin says the same sex renounced/denied it, not that it opened her; English reverses the sense.

problems.fix: Remove the erroneous citation or replace with the correct reference.
problems.ruling: Exodus 13:2 reads 'sanctum Domino' matching the Latin; the verse is correctly cited and not wrong.

fixed: Changed 'the same sex opened her' to 'the same sex renounced it' because the Latin 'idem illud sexus resignavit' means the sex renounced or denied it, not that it opened her.
Removed the erroneous citation '(Exodus 13:2)' because the quoted verse 'Omne masculinum adaperiens vulvam sanctum vocabitur domino' is not found in Exodus 13:2.

problems.why: 'resignavit' means 'sealed/stamped' here, not 'renounced'; the sex stamped its mark on the opened body.
problems.fix: that same sex stamped its mark upon it.
problems.ruling: source 'idem illud sexus resignavit' uses resignavit = 'to seal/mark', translation 'the same sex renounced it' misstates meaning

edits.new: that same sex stamped its mark upon it

fixed: Changed 'the same sex renounced it' to 'that same sex stamped its mark upon it': source 'idem illud sexus resignavit' uses 'resignavit' in the sense of 'unsealed/stamped', not 'renounced'.

problems.quote: that same sex stamped its mark upon it
problems.why: Latin says the sex renounced/rejected it, not that it stamped a mark.
problems.fix: that same sex also renounced it
problems.ruling: resignavit here means 'renounced/rejected,' not 'stamped a mark'; translator confused resignavit with signavit, changing meaning.

edits.old: that same sex stamped its mark upon it

fixed: The Latin 'idem illud sexus resignavit' means 'that same sex renounced it' (resignavit = renounced, unsealed, gave up), not 'stamped its mark upon it'. The earlier edit to 'the same sex renounced it' was correct; the later change to 'stamped its mark upon it' was wrong.

problems.why: Tertullian uses 'flesh' (caro) and 'body' (corpus) technically distinct but often interchangeably; reader cannot track when distinction matters.
problems.fix: Note when 'body' means soma/corpus vs. when 'flesh' means sarx/caro.

problems.quote: Certainly she must be called not a virgin rather than a virgin, by a certain leap a mother before she was married
problems.why: Paradox intentionally, but 'not a virgin rather than a virgin' is opaque; 'by a certain leap' is obscure.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'She became a mother before becoming a wife, thus in one sense not a virgin.'

problems.quote: the nuptial passion of the opened womb
problems.why: 'Passion' suggests suffering or sexual passion; here means 'event/occurrence' or 'passage through.'
problems.fix: Use 'the marital event of the opened womb' or clarify.

problems.quote: Every male opening the womb will be called holy to the Lord
problems.why: Exodus 13:2 / Luke 2:23; but 'opening the womb' (πᾶν ἄρσεν διανοῖγον μήτραν) is standard. Tertullian applies to Christ's unique birth.

problems.quote: Every male opening the womb will be called holy to the Lord
problems.why: No scripture reference is given; the allusion is to Exodus 13:2 or Luke 2:23, but the reader cannot identify it.

problems.quote: We do read in Ezekiel about that cow which bore and did not bear.
problems.why: No specific Ezekiel reference is given, and the allusion is obscure; the reader cannot locate it.
problems.fix: Add reference, e.g., '(Ezekiel 4:1-3)' or clarify the passage being alluded to.

problems.quote: in her giving birth she married
problems.why: The word 'married' is misleading; the argument is that her virginity was physically ended by childbirth, not that she entered a marriage.
problems.fix: Use 'lost her virginity' or 'was physically opened' instead of 'married.'

problems.quote: Certainly she must be called not a virgin rather than a virgin, by a certain leap a mother before she was married.
problems.why: The phrase 'by a certain leap a mother before she was married' does not make sense in English; 'leap' is puzzling.
problems.fix: Rewrite: 'she became a mother before she was married, by a kind of leap.'

problems.quote: Yet it does not follow that she did not bear, or that she was a virgin who was not a virgin, because she was not a mother from her own inward parts.
problems.source_quote: non tamen ut ideo non peperit, et ideo virgo quae non virgo, quia non de visceribus suis mater.
problems.why: The quia-clause is the rejected ground, not Tertullian's claim that she was not a mother from her own inward parts.
problems.fix: Not so that she therefore did not bear, and was therefore a virgin who was not a virgin, on the ground that she was not a mother from her own inward parts.
problems.ruling: Source 'non tamen ut ideo non peperit, et ideo virgo quae non virgo, quia non de visceribus suis mater' – quia-clause is the rejected ground; English reads as Tertullian's assertion, reversing sense.

problems.source_quote: Omne masculinum adaperiens vulvam sanctum vocabitur domino.
problems.why: This formula is Luke 2:23. Exodus 13:2 does not say every male will be called holy to the Lord.
problems.fix: Every male opening the womb will be called holy to the Lord (Luke 2:23).
problems.ruling: 'Omne masculinum adaperiens vulvam sanctum vocabitur domino' is the Luke 2:23 wording (quoting Exodus 13:2); Exodus 13:2 lacks 'called holy', so the citation is imprecise and misleading.

last_rejected.why: Latin says "Est est" (is is), not "yes is yes"; adds a word not in source.
last_rejected.ruling: Tertullian echoes Matt 5:37; 'Est est' = 'yes yes' idiomatically. Translation within acceptable range.

last_rejected.source_quote: Lux lux, et Tenebrae tenehrae, et Est est, et Non non; quod amplius, hoc a malo est.
last_rejected.why: The source provides no citation; adding Matthew 5:37 is incorrect.
last_rejected.fix: remove the citation; keep the statement without a biblical reference
last_rejected.ruling: Source 'quod amplius hoc a malo est' directly alludes to Matt 5:37; parenthetical citation is standard scholarly practice.

last_rejected.why: idem illud is neuter object: sex unsealed that same thing. English attaches 'same' to sex.
last_rejected.ruling: "idem illud sexus resignavit" is ambiguous; "idem illud" can be nominative subject ("that same sex"), as English reads it. Sense is unchanged either way.
